title: Filed ITR-4 last year? You might need to switch to ITR-3 in AY 2026-27
description: Filing ITR-4 for Assessment Year (AY) 2025-26 does not automatically qualify you for ITR-4 in AY 2026-27. Changes in your income sources or business activitie.

faq.a: Presumptive taxation is a simplified scheme under the Income Tax Act where eligible small businesses and professionals can declare their income at a prescribed rate (e.g., 6%, 8%, or 50% of turnover/receipts) without maintaining detailed books of accounts.

faq.q: Can I file ITR-3 if I have only salary income?
faq.a: No, ITR-3 is specifically for individuals and HUFs with income from business or profession. If you only have salary income, you would typically file ITR-1 (Sahaj) or ITR-2, depending on other income sources like capital gains or multiple house properties.

faq.q: What happens if my business turnover crosses ₹2 crores but I still file ITR-4?
faq.a: If your business turnover exceeds ₹2 crores, you are no longer eligible for presumptive taxation under Section 44AD and cannot file ITR-4. Filing ITR-4 in such a scenario would make your return defective and could lead to penalties and interest.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to maintain books of accounts if I switch to ITR-3?
faq.a: Yes, if you file ITR-3 because you are not opting for presumptive taxation or are otherwise ineligible for ITR-4, you are generally required to maintain proper books of accounts as per Section 44AA of the Income Tax Act. These books may also need to be audited under Section 44AB if your turnover exceeds specified limits.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) file ITR-4 or ITR-3?
faq.a: NRIs are generally not eligible to file ITR-4 (Sugam). They typically need to file ITR-2 if they have only salary, house property, capital gains, or other income. If an NRI has income from a business or profession in India, they would need to file ITR-3.

faq.q: What if I filed ITR-4 but later realise I had capital gains?
faq.a: If you realise after filing ITR-4 that you had income from capital gains, your filed return is defective. You should file a revised return using ITR-3, provided the deadline for revised returns has not passed. Failure to do so can lead to penalties.

faq.q: What is the deadline for filing ITR for AY 2026-27?
faq.a: For most individual taxpayers, the deadline for filing ITR for Assessment Year 2026-27 (income earned in FY 2025-26) is typically July 31, 2026. However, this date can vary for businesses requiring an audit or certain other categories of taxpayers.

fact_check.summary: The article provides a largely accurate and comprehensive overview of ITR-4 and ITR-3 eligibility, particularly highlighting triggers for switching between the forms. Some specific numerical thresholds for presumptive taxation have been updated in recent budgets, which the article correctly reflects in some places but misses in others, leading to minor inaccuracies. The information on penalties and defective returns is generally correct.

corrections.note: No changes were made as the fact-checker's note could not be verified against authoritative sources, and the original statement remains accurate based on current verifiable information.

edits.why: The fact-checker's note states that for AY 2026-27, ITR-4 allows reporting income from up to two house properties. However, the provided source does not support this claim. The Income Tax Department's official ITR-4 instructions for AY 2024-25 (which would be relevant for FY 2023-24, informing AY 2024-25 and subsequent years unless changed) consistently state that ITR-4 is for individuals with income from 'One House Property (excluding cases where loss is brought forward from previous years or to be carried forward to subsequent years)'. There is no indication of a change to allow two house properties for AY 2026-27 in the authoritative sources. Therefore, the original statement remains accurate based on current verifiable information.
